title: Firgrove Logistics — inventory assistant onramp notes
content:
Quick capture from discovery call with Firgrove Logistics (Samantha R., CTO; Marco L., Platform lead) — intake scratchpad. Do not share externally yet.

Summary (one-liner): Firgrove wants an on-prem/private deployment of an LLM-backed inventory assistant for warehouse operators and planners. Primary constraints: sub-400ms 1-shot lookup latency for barcode->context answers, strict PII isolation, and integration with their legacy WMS (SOAP API + nightly delta CSVs).

Attendees: Samantha Reeves (CTO), Marco Lopez (Platform), Elena Park (Ops manager), Daniel Vega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood solutions eng)

High-level goals:
- Real-time forklift/operator lookups at dock: human asks "where is SKU 7F-23?" and gets shelf + age + suggested replen rule.
- Natural language QA for planners ("what SKUs are below safety stock in warehouse B?").
- Audit trail & redaction (no customer PII should be surfaced).
- On-prem control plane or VPC-private with customer-managed KMS.

Non-functional constraints / must-haves:
- PII/data residency: entire payload must stay on their network. No hosted inference.
- Latency SLO: 95p <= 400ms for single-turn queries from dock terminals (80% are short, 1–2 token system prompts + user text ~32–64 tokens).
- Throughput: peak 60 rps across 12 warehouses during shift change (burst tolerant).
- Model privacy: prefer open model (license review) or Redwood-managed private model variants — customer legal wants attribution on model weights.

System integration notes / gotchas:
- WMS exposes SOAP endpoints for current inventory and a nightly bulk CSV dump with full SKU metadata. Need a connector that can do incremental updates; try to avoid full reloads every hour.
- Barcode scanners push to an in-house MQ (RabbitMQ on site). Recommend building a small adapter to forward relevant messages to the inference tier.
- Warehouse terminals are thin clients (Chromeboxes) on 4G backup links — fallbacks to cached responses required for offline mode.
- Firewall rules: customer only allows outbound HTTPS to a whitelist; if we do a Private deployment, control plane traffic must be over their VPN.

Model / runtime considerations (initial thoughts):
- Use small/medium open LLM (e.g., 7B–13B) with quantization (8-bit) to meet latency/cost; profile on their Nvidia T4-equivalent nodes first.
- Enable KV cache for repeated SKU lookups per session to reduce average latency/token cost.
- Keep prompt template minimal. Use a compact system prompt that encodes domain schema (fields: location, qty, last_moved_ts, age_days, replen_rule).
- Consider hybrid approach: rules engine + small LLM for ambiguous QA (LLM for mapping fuzzy queries to structured queries, then run deterministic WMS lookup). This will reduce hallucination risk.

Security / compliance notes:
- KMS integration: they use HashiCorp Vault HSM. Redwood Private should support customer KMS key wrapping and audit logging.
- Audit log retention: Ops asks for 90 days of searchable traces (token-level redaction required).
- PII removal: need a pre-processor to strip passenger/customer names and phone numbers from free text. Build redaction regex + small model-based PII detector for edge cases.

Preliminary deployment plan (phased):
1) PoC (2–4 weeks): single warehouse, one inference node, tiny model (7B) quantized, sync adapter from WMS nightly dump, manual verification of redaction rules. Test latency with real dock queries.
2) Pilot (6–8 weeks): expand to 3 warehouses, integrate RabbitMQ adapter for live barcode events, add prefix/KV caching, integrate Vault for keys, basic SLO monitoring in Redwood Console.
3) Production rollout (quarterly): autoscaling pools, canary rollout policies, A/B prompt variants, long-term log retention and compliance handoff.

Open questions to resolve with customer:
- SLA expectations for private deployments (ops vs sales). Samantha says they expect "enterprise-level" SLAs but want cost predictability.
- Hardware on prem: confirm GPU class (T4 vs A10 vs A30) and available RAM per node. Marco to share infra inventory by 2025-03-04.
- WMS schema mapping: need a sample CSV (nightly export) and SOAP WSDL to prototype connector. Elena to provide by 2025-02-25 (pending).
- Offline/edge plan: what is acceptable user experience when control plane unreachable? Define degrade modes.

Action items (who / by when):
- Marco: share GPU/inventory + network egress rules (2025-03-04).
- Elena: sample nightly CSV + example SOAP call / WSDL (2025-02-25) — BLOCKER for connector dev.
- Daniel: prepare PoC estimate (instance sizing, model choice, storage, KMS integration) and draft pilot runbook (2025-02-28).
- Priya: draft prompt templates and redaction heuristics; run small local PII detection tests (2025-03-03).
- Jonah: spike on RabbitMQ adapter with a lightweight forwarder to the local inference endpoint (2025-03-07).

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: hallucinations returning incorrect shelf locations. Mitigation: enforce deterministic lookup path for any response that includes a location — map LLM output to a structured query and validate against WMS before responding.
- Risk: latency spikes under shift-change bursts. Mitigation: pre-warm dedicated capacity, set burst/queueing policies in Redwood Dedicated/Private, and use short-circuit cache for top-100 SKUs per warehouse.
- Risk: legal model license concerns. Mitigation: prepare an options matrix (open-weight models we can ship vs Redwood-verified private weights) and pass to legal for review.

Notes to SE team (internal):
- Keep the PoC small and deterministic: focus on mapping-to-query + validation loop. Avoid letting LLM craft free-form addresses unless validated.
- Instrument trace IDs in barcode flow so we can correlate dock terminal event -> LLM prompt -> WMS query -> final response for debugging.
- Prepare a small acceptance checklist for Elena: redaction verified on 50 sample free-text queries, 95p latency < 400ms under synthetic 20rps load.

Misc (raw fragments):
- "If SKU unknown, return 'unknown sku' and suggested next steps (check shelf, escalate to inventory ops)" — Elena prefers explicit failure modes.
- Consider embedding based nearest-neighbor for fuzzy product name resolution (search index updated nightly).

Next meeting: schedule follow-up to review infra inventory + sample CSVs. Propose Tue 2025-03-11 10am PT.

-- End of scratchpad --

(Keep this in users drive only; move to shared_drives once legal sign-off and pilot paperwork complete.)
